approach: Fix it where the duplicate is made: `Athena::retry` (reading.rs). After the registry is reaped, it refuses an interrupted job (Dispatched, no live process) that already has a standing retry. A standing retry is found through `job_history`/`retried_job` by one new helper, `retries_by_job`, which maps each job to its newest retry that still stands for the work: a retry closed unrun (dropped, declined, abandoned, stale) is ignored. One more helper, `retry_follow_up`, says what to do next from the retry's state (go, correct, retry, wait, or nothing); the refusal and `athena status` both use it. Status adds `retried_as` to the job line and replaces the `athena retry <old>` hint with `retried as <new>`. The state string stays "interrupted". The drain's `run_job`/`attempts` is changed so that an interrupted item whose retry was recorded without a reading (reader failed) is read again through the retry job (`go`, the existing Unread path), not retried a second time. Tests: retry.rs (double retry, status text, dropped retry, dead process, rejected twice) and tests/drain.rs (dead registry entry listed and retried by the drain; unread retry read again). CHANGELOG entry.

decisions.choice: Refuse in Athena::retry (reading.rs 1101), after `registry().reap()` and the pause check and before preflight/`ask`, only when `job.state()==Dispatched && !self.running(id)` and `retries_by_job(&records)` has an entry for the id. `reap()` is moved up from line 1116 (replaced, not duplicated).
decisions.reason: The request and the root-cause default put the check in retry itself. Limiting it to interrupted jobs leaves retries of rejected, failed and timed-out jobs as they are (out of scope). Reaping first makes a dead registry entry count as interrupted, which is the restart case.

rejected.why: It is also called when a retry job is read again (reading.rs 1043 `read_unread` path and 1230), so a retry job would find itself as 'an existing retry' and refuse its own re-read. It would also change `ask`.
A script or the user calling `athena retry <id>` directly would still start the same work twice (root-cause default).

decisions.choice: New `pub fn retries_by_job(records:&Records) -> BTreeMap<String,String>` next to `job_history` (reading.rs ~1535). It walks `job_history(records)` (newest first; `request_jobs` sorts descending), skips a retry whose job state is `Closed(Dropped|Declined|Abandoned|Stale|Closed)` (closed without standing for the work), and keeps the first remaining retry per `retry_of` target. A retry that is proposed, queued, declined-but-open, dispatched, blocked, rejected, failed, timed out or landed stands.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 1: a retry the user closed unrun (`close_with` records Proposed/Queued as Dropped, Declined as Declined, manage.rs 103-115) must not block the old job, because retrying a dropped job is refused by `earlier_attempt_with` (reading.rs 1343-1355) and the old job would be stuck. Both retry and status call one helper, so they cannot disagree. It reuses `retried_job` through `job_history` (criterion 5): no new parse of 'try again on'.

rejected.option: Count every 'try again on <id>' job whatever its state (the round-1 design)
rejected.why: Leaves the old job stuck behind a dropped retry; status would name a dead job.
It holds ids only, with no new id for the message, and counts dropped retries too. Left unchanged; the drain does not list a job that has any later retry, so it never duplicates.

rejected.option: Re-parse RETRY_PREFIX in retry or status
rejected.why: Could drift from `retry_reference`; criterion 5 forbids it.

decisions.choice: New `pub fn retry_follow_up(records:&Records, retry:&str, running:bool) -> String` in reading.rs that names the next step from the retry's state: Queued/Proposed/Blocked → ``athena go <new>``; Declined → ``athena correct <new> "<line>"``; Dispatched and running → 'it is running; wait for it'; Dispatched not running → 'it was interrupted too; ``athena retry <new>``'; Closed Rejected/Failed/TimedOut → ``athena retry <new>``; Closed Landed → 'it landed; nothing is left to do'; anything else → 'see ``athena status``'. The refusal reads: `job {old} was interrupted and was already retried as job {new} ({state}); {follow_up}. Nothing was started.` Status uses the same text.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4: the right next step depends on the retry's state.

rejected.why: Wrong when the retry was rejected or failed: the next step is `athena retry <new>`.

decisions.choice: Keep `JobLine.state` = 'interrupted'; add `retried_as: Option<String>` (skipped in JSON when None), set in `status()` only for an interrupted job with an entry in `retries_by_job`; for such a job skip the disk-hold text. In the next list the interrupted arm with `retried_as` pushes `retried as {new} ({state})   # {follow_up} · or: athena close {old} --why "..." (commits what the interrupted job left)` instead of the `athena retry {old}` line. display.rs `plan_suffix` appends ` · retried as {new}`.
decisions.reason: Existing readers test `state == "interrupted"` (status.rs 1698, 1707; display.rs 899; lifecycle.rs 1926/1971; binary.rs 327-340; run/tests.rs 2223) and `jobs_by_state`; a new state string would break them. An optional field is additive.

rejected.why: Breaks those consumers and the 'existing tests unchanged' criterion.

rejected.option: Drop the retry line with no replacement
rejected.why: The user would get no guidance for the interrupted job.

decisions.choice: Change the drain (answers finding 2, option (a)). In `Drain::run_job` (drain.rs 1555-1568) a read from `ReadOf::Retry` that returns a job with a reader error now takes the unread path: `RunStep::Unread` becomes a struct variant `Unread { reason, retried: Option<String> }`, `retried` being the new job when the read was a retry. In `attempts` (drain.rs 1823-1834), on `Unread` with `retried: Some(job)`, set `*last_job = job` and `retry = false`, then continue; the next attempt is `ReadOf::Queued(job)`, so `go` reads the retry job again (`go_job` Proposed with no reading → `read_unread`, run/mod.rs 388-390, which accepts the still-interrupted old job through `earlier_attempt_with(.., &|j| self.running(j))`, reading.rs 1043). The existing `unread >= 2` rule still skips the item after two empty readings.
decisions.reason: Today a retry whose reader fails leaves `retry` true and `last_job` unchanged (drain.rs 1844-1848), so the next attempt calls `athena.retry(<old>)` again and, before this change, made a duplicate retry job; with the guard it would be refused and the item would end failed. Reading the already recorded retry job again does the work once and is the path queued jobs already use.

rejected.option: State that the refusal is the intended end of the drain item (option (b))
rejected.why: The item would end failed with a refusal although a retry job exists that only needs reading; the drain's goal is to do the work once.
Round-1 claimed the guard never fires in the drain; it fires on this path.

decisions.reason: The request names `reap()` in reading.rs and in drain.rs; each is exercised by its own entry point (`Athena::status`/`retry`; the drain's `RealSteps::queue`, drain.rs 3496, and `drain::drain`). An exited child's pid is dead by construction; a fixed large pid could be alive.

rejected.option: Leave the drain's reap untested and say why

risks.risk: The guard refuses a legitimate retry, for example when the first retry was closed unrun and the user wants a fresh one.
risks.mitigation: `retries_by_job` ignores retries closed as Dropped, Declined, Abandoned, Stale or Closed, so such a retry no longer blocks. `a_dropped_retry_does_not_block_a_new_retry` shows it. risks.risk: The drain change alters an existing drain flow: an unread retry used to be retried again.
risks.mitigation: The branch is taken only when a retry read returns both a job and an error, which no Stub-based test produces; the queued-unread tests keep `retried: None`. The new drain test covers the changed path against the real `Athena::retry`. The producer runs the whole drain test file.

risks.risk: `go` on the unread retry job may not accept the old interrupted job in some state, so the second read fails again.

risks.risk: The old interrupted job stays dispatched with a 'retried as' line, because its records are not closed.
risks.mitigation: Out of scope by the brief. The refusal and status offer `athena close <old> --why "..."` and name the retry's own next step.

risks.mitigation: Add `retried_as: None` in `job_line` and in the one display.rs test literal; `cargo test --locked` compiles every test.
